newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, November 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, November 20.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi detailed plans to raise a 12.5 trillion lire "Euro-tax". The government intends to collect 5.5 trillion from additional income taxes, which should be partly reimbursed in 1999. Trade unions said they are satisfied, but employers association Confindustria and shopkeepers criticised the plan along with centre-right opposition (all).
* Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema said the government should not be conditioned by hard-left Communist Refoundation party (all).
* Cuban leader Fidel Castro paid an historic 35 minute visit to Pope Jean Paul. The Pope accepted an invitation to go to Cuba next year (all).
* An article in French newspaper Le Monde quoted government sources saying the Bank of Italy is selling lire to avoid it re-entering the ERM at a too strong level (all).

* Three Italian and three foreign institutions have expressed an interest in the sale of 60 percent of stock in Banco di Napoli. Treasury-owned bank Mediocredito Centrale is seeking an agreement with Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and insurance group Ina, who joined forces to present an offer (Sole 24 Ore).
* Car maker Fiat rose 4.7 percent on the stock market, as Foreign trade minister Augusto Fantozzi said the government is considering help for the car industry (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
